subject: Lyra renewal: bakeoff holdout, capacity uplift & term bridge
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@lyra.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal planning: Lyra bakeoff window + mutual action plan

Samir —

Thanks for the quick chat yesterday. Based on our notes, Lyra's enterprise renewal is up in October and I understand your team is running a formal bakeoff to validate throughput/latency and unit-cost across the contenders. We want to make this as frictionless as possible.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood runs a full-day benchmark on your sample workload (we'll bring identical model variants we expect would be used in production)
- We publish a concise benchmark report (p99 latency, mean throughput, token unit cost, degradation under concurrency)
- Based on results, we align on a term bridge: capacity uplift + pricing tiers for a 12-month commitment

Can we schedule the benchmark week of Sep 6? If procurement has a requirements packet, please send it over (I attached the brief checklist so we can confirm environment/keys).

Attachments: lyra_bakeoff_requirements.pdf

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@lyra.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@lyra.ai>, procurement@lyra.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: Lyra bakeoff window + mutual action plan

Priyom —

Appreciate the outreach. Procurement wants the bakeoff to include: sustained throughput for our peak 90th percentile, p99 tail under 500ms target for our 128-token avg prompts, and a cost-per-1M-tokens calc that includes expected caching behavior. Also need an ops runbook for fallback behavior if a variant underperforms.

We are currently in a holdout stance with one other vendor who claims a sub-300ms p99; if Redwood can show a consistent profile at scale and give predictable pricing for the uplift we're evaluating, we can move the renewal conversation quickly.

I'll send the full requirements doc from procurement in a follow-up. Tentatively OK for the week of Sep 6 but procurement would like to see a proposed pricing bridge and any concessions you might offer for a 12-month committed uplift.

--
Samir Patel
VP Platforms, Lyra.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@lyra.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 11:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: Lyra bakeoff window + mutual action plan

Samir —

Thanks. We reviewed your high-level asks and put together a recommended benchmark plan + a commercial bridge for the renewal. Highlights:

Benchmark plan (attachment: redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf)
- Full-run with your representative workload (same prompt mix you shared)
- Measurements: p50/p90/p99 latency, mean throughput, sustained 30m & 4h windows, and cost-per-1M-calculated both with and without KV/prefix cache enabled
- Ops runbook: automatic region failover + model-variant fallback; we'll run a simulated failover during the test

Commercial bridge (summary)
- 12-month committed uplift: 2x current reserved capacity (measured in GPU-hours), with tiered unit pricing: 0–1x (current) = standard, 1–2x = 12% discount, >2x eligible for additional negotiation
- Early pilot concession: first 3 months at a 20% reduced list price on the uplift bucket to de-risk migration (this is time-limited)
- SLA: target p99 latency of 450ms for the configured variant. If we miss targets twice in a quarter we propose a credit mechanism (details to be included in SOW)

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf

If this looks aligned, we'll aim to run the benchmark on Sep 7 and finalize a DocuSign-ready SOW within 48 hours of a positive report. Deal ID: DEAL-2027-0892.

Two asks for you:
1) Can procurement confirm the Windows/IP allowlist and sample dataset availability by Sep 2?
2) Can you share the target 1M-token cost ceiling (ballpark) so we can model pricing tiers?

Best,
Priyom
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2027 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Lyra renewal: bakeoff holdout, capacity uplift & term bridge

Forwarding the thread — Lyra is explicitly in a holdout with a competitor claiming better p99s at scale. Priyom proposed a 12-month 2x uplift with a 3-month pilot concession (20% off uplift). Need quick guidance on:

- Margin impact of the 3-month pilot at that uplift level (Marissa)
- Appropriateness of SLA credit language and whether we should tighten the p99 target (Jordan)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Lyra renewal: bakeoff holdout, capacity uplift & term bridge

Karthik —

Reviewed. We can approve the commercial bridge with the following controls to protect margin and risk:

- Approve the 3-month pilot concession at 20% off the uplift bucket, but cap the absolute uplift eligible for the pilot to 1.5x current reserved (not full 2x)
- Post-pilot, uplift transitions to the tiered pricing defined by Priyom (12% discount 1–2x). If Lyra requests >2x we require a separate commercial review and exec sign-off
- Approve the SLA language but tighten the p99 target to 425ms for the configured variant; include explicit remediation steps for a failed simulated failover

I'll attach the proposed pricing spreadsheet and redline suggestions for the SOW. Once we get positive benchmark numbers, Jordan can finalize the SLA verbiage and I will sign off on pricing to enable Priyom to send a DocuSign.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_tiers.xlsx

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@lyra.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@lyra.ai>, procurement@lyra.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 10:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Lyra renewal: bakeoff holdout, capacity uplift & term bridge

Priyom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for being flexible on commercial structure. Procurement reviewed Marissa's constraints and are comfortable proceeding with the benchmark on Sep 7 under the capped pilot uplift (1.5x) and the tightened p99 target (425ms).

Next steps for us:
- Execute benchmark on Sep 7 per your plan
- If results meet targets, legal/procurement will review the SOW; please send DocuSign-ready SOW with the agreed caps and credit language

Please send the DocuSign link when ready. We have one more internal stakeholder (CISO) who will review the ops runbook; Olivia will coordinate that review with you.

DocuSign request: procurement asked for a single SOW that includes the pilot concession and a follow-on committed pricing schedule.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Samir
VP Platforms, Lyra.ai

Attachments: docusign_lyra_sow.pdf
